title: 70% of Old Shanghai Lived Behind This Stone Gate | China Travel Expert
description:
Skip the skyline for a minute. From the 1850s to the 1940s, around 70% of Shanghainese lived here — in the lane houses behind a stone-arch gate.

The gate is called shikumen (石库门), "stone-framed gate." The alleys branching off the main lane are the longtang (弄堂). It's a hybrid the city invented: a Western terraced-house frame wrapped around Chinese courtyard life. Because the houses were small, life spilled outside — bamboo poles hung heavy with laundry overhead, breakfast stalls fired up before dawn, and neighbors chatted on little stools in the lane. It's the most everyday, most human side of Shanghai, and it's still there behind the towers.

🧭 Expert Tip: Go around 7am — the lane wakes up with breakfast carts and residents, not tour groups.

旧时七成上海人，都住在这道石库门后的弄堂里。
